Subject: p99 spikes + 502s since 09:00 - DataForge prod

Team —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latencies and a small number of 502 errors on our hosted endpoints beginning ~09:00 PDT this morning. Summary:
- p50 ~ 80ms, p95 jumped from ~320ms to ~1.2s, p99 spikes up to ~3.8s in bursts.
- Throughput stayed steady; traffic pattern unchanged.
- We saw a handful of 502/504s coincident with the worst spikes.

We pulled the request_id list and attached a tar with traces and a few model run snapshots (dataforge_p99_snapshot.tar.gz). Hoping you can triage — this is impacting a small set of high-SLA customers and our ops team is getting pressure.

Requesting: immediate triage + an ETA for mitigation or a temporary routing/workaround. If this is a capacity issue we may accept a short-term routing to dedicated nodes while you investigate.

Kari

Thanks for the data, Kari — initial triage notes below. I'm putting together a longer dump but want to call out what I see so far.

What I observed:
- NVML traces in your snapshot show transient OOM throttles on worker GPUs followed by process restarts. The sequence correlates with p99 spikes.
- Memory utilization is high but not sustained; instead, we see rapid allocations+frees that match a fragmentation pattern (many small allocations, inability to reclaim contiguous pages).
- KV cache behavior: your workload has many short-context requests which causes frequent KV cache churn. When combined with our current allocation policy this can trigger fragmentation that leads to soft OOMs under bursty tails.

Immediate mitigations (ordered by speed to implement):
A) Route heavy tail requests for the affected model to a dedicated pod template (reserved capacity) until we patch allocation strategy — this is the fastest short-term fix and we can do it for a rolling 2–4 hour window.
B) Swap to an alternative model variant we have that uses a smaller working set (quantized fp16/8 variant) — needs a quick config change and validation (10–30m).
C) Apply a runtime allocation tweak (reduce max fragmentation threshold + disable eager page reuse) — requires rollout and small risk; estimate 2–4 hours for safe canary.

I'm attaching the NVML trace extract I'm working from (nvml-trace-20261011.txt) and a short diagnostic profile (model_kv_cache_profile.json).

I recommend A or B as a temporary measure, then we schedule a patch (C) to address the fragmentation cause. I'll coordinate logs and a postmortem draft.

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: nvml-trace-20261011.txt]
[Attachment: model_kv_cache_profile.json]
